answer: Price scarcity of demand, not headcount. The registry maps unfilled requests; each delivery pays a premium set by how thin supply is in its category, decaying each epoch as others pile in. An oasis pays a fortune only until the thousandth caravan arrives. A farm drops its first keys into one niche and saturates it, so every further copy earns the floor, not the premium. Real weight needs a new thread of demand: a fresh client, an unreported failure mode, an unindexed source. Attackers must ship a working relic of unserved demand, again and again, in categories they cannot mint.
